0.short: A first step taken in trust. The Fool is the start of every journey, open to whatever the road may bring.
0.long: The Fool stands at the edge of something new with nothing but curiosity and an open heart. Numbered zero, this card belongs to no single place in the deck and so can begin anywhere. It speaks of fresh starts, spontaneity and the courage to leap before every answer is known. When The Fool appears, life is inviting you to trust the moment, to travel light and to let experience be your teacher. Not every risk is reckless, and some doors only open for those willing to walk through them without a map. Its shadow is carelessness: a leap made without looking, or a refusal to take any responsibility for where the path leads. Read with care, The Fool reminds you that beginnings are sacred, and that a little innocence is a strength, not a weakness.

1.short: Will turned into action. The Magician has every tool at hand and the focus to make an idea real.
1.long: The Magician gathers the four elements of the tarot, fire, water, air and earth, and directs them with intention. This is the card of skill, resourcefulness and personal power. What you need is already within reach; the task is to focus it. When The Magician appears, the moment favours action: begin the project, have the conversation, make the plan concrete. Ideas become real through attention and practice, and this card says you are capable of both. Its shadow side warns of talent used to manipulate, or of energy scattered across too many directions at once. The Magician asks a simple question: what will you create with what you have been given? The answer starts with a single, deliberate act.

2.short: The keeper of hidden knowledge. The High Priestess asks you to be still and listen to your intuition.
2.long: The High Priestess sits between the seen and the unseen, guardian of the mysteries that cannot be spoken aloud. She is intuition, inner knowing and the quiet wisdom that arrives when the mind is calm. When she appears, the answer you seek will not come from more information or more effort. It is already within you, waiting beneath the surface. Pay attention to dreams, to instincts and to what feels true before you can explain why. This is a card of patience: not every truth is ready to be revealed, and some things are learned only by waiting. In her shadow she can signal secrets kept too long, or a disconnection from your own inner voice. Her lesson is trust: in yourself, and in the timing of what is still unfolding.

3.short: Abundance, nurture and creative life. The Empress brings growth to everything she touches.
3.long: The Empress is the great mother of the tarot, the card of fertility, beauty and abundance in every form. She governs the natural world and the pleasures of the senses, and she reminds you that growth needs care, comfort and time. When she appears, something in your life is ready to flourish: a relationship, a creative work, a home or a sense of self. This is a call to nurture, to create and to receive as well as to give. Rest, beauty and pleasure are not indulgences here; they are how life renews itself. In her shadow she may point to neglect of your own needs, or to care that has turned into smothering. The Empress teaches that what is tended with love will grow, in its own season.

4.short: Structure, authority and steady leadership. The Emperor builds order where there was chaos.
4.long: The Emperor sits on a throne of stone, the image of stability, discipline and lasting structure. Where The Empress nurtures, The Emperor protects and organises. He represents authority, responsibility and the wisdom of experience. When he appears, it is time to bring order to your situation: set boundaries, make a plan and take ownership of your decisions. Strength here comes from consistency rather than force. The card may also point to a father figure, a mentor or an institution that shapes your path. In his shadow The Emperor becomes rigid, controlling or cold, holding on to power for its own sake. At his best he shows that true leadership creates safety, and that a strong foundation is what allows everything else to grow.

5.short: Tradition, teaching and shared belief. The High Priest links you to wisdom handed down through time.
5.long: The High Priest is the teacher and keeper of tradition, the bridge between the sacred and everyday life. He stands for established values, spiritual guidance and the communities that hold knowledge together. When he appears, you may be learning from a mentor, joining a group, or returning to rituals and beliefs that ground you. There is wisdom in what has been tested by time, and this card invites you to honour it. It can also mark commitments made in public, such as vows, ceremonies and formal learning. In his shadow The High Priest warns of conformity without thought, or rules followed only because they are rules. His deeper lesson is to understand a tradition well enough to know which parts to keep, and which to question with respect.

6.short: Love, union and a choice made from the heart. The Lovers ask what you truly value.
6.long: The Lovers is a card of deep connection, between two people, or between the different parts of yourself. It speaks of love, harmony and attraction, but also of choice. At its heart this card asks you to decide what you value most, and to align your actions with it. When The Lovers appear, a relationship may be deepening, or you may stand at a crossroads where the heart must lead. Honest communication and mutual respect are the foundation of any union this card blesses. In its shadow it can show imbalance, temptation, or a choice avoided for too long. The Lovers remind you that true connection begins with being honest with yourself, and that the right choice is the one you can stand behind with your whole heart.

7.short: Victory through willpower and focus. The Chariot moves forward when opposing forces are held in balance.
7.long: The Chariot is the card of determination, momentum and hard won success. Its driver holds two opposing forces in balance and steers them toward a single goal. When The Chariot appears, you have the strength to overcome obstacles, provided you stay focused and keep your direction clear. This is not a time for hesitation. Gather your resolve, trust your discipline and move forward with confidence. The card often marks progress, travel, or a challenge met head on. In its shadow it warns of a loss of control, aggression, or pushing ahead without knowing where you are going. The Chariot teaches that victory belongs to those who master themselves first, and that the reins are held with steadiness, not force.

8.short: Quiet courage and gentle mastery. Strength shows that compassion can tame what force cannot.
8.long: Strength is a card of inner power, the kind that does not need to shout. Its image is a calm hand resting on a lion, mastering wild energy through patience and compassion rather than force. When Strength appears, you are being asked to meet a challenge with courage and a steady heart. This may mean facing fear, managing difficult emotions, or showing kindness where anger would be easier. True strength here is resilience: the ability to stay soft without breaking. The card also speaks of confidence that comes from self acceptance. In its shadow it can point to self doubt, or to feelings pushed down rather than understood. Strength reminds you that you are braver than you think, and that gentleness is a power of its own.

9.short: Solitude, reflection and the inner light. The Hermit steps away from noise to find the truth.
9.long: The Hermit walks alone, carrying a lantern that lights only the next step of the path. This card speaks of solitude, introspection and the search for meaning. When The Hermit appears, it is time to withdraw a little from the noise of the world and listen inward. Answers will come through reflection, study or quiet contemplation rather than through action or advice from others. The Hermit can also appear as a guide or teacher who has walked the road before you. Solitude here is not loneliness; it is a chosen retreat that restores clarity. In its shadow the card can signal isolation that has gone on too long, or a withdrawal that avoids life rather than understands it. The Hermit's light is wisdom earned, and it is meant to be shared once found.

10.short: Cycles, chance and turning points. The Wheel of Fortune reminds you that nothing stays the same.
10.long: The Wheel of Fortune turns without pause, carrying everything through cycles of rise and fall. It is the card of fate, timing and change. When it appears, a turning point is near: circumstances are shifting, often in ways you did not plan. Luck may be moving in your favour, and an opportunity may arrive unexpectedly. The deeper message is that life moves in seasons, and that no moment, good or difficult, lasts forever. What you can control is how you meet each turn of the wheel. In its shadow the card can point to resistance to change, or to a sense of being at the mercy of events. The Wheel of Fortune asks you to stay open, to adapt and to trust that every ending carries the seed of what comes next.

11.short: Truth, fairness and cause and effect. Justice weighs every choice and asks for honesty.
11.long: Justice holds a sword in one hand and scales in the other, the image of clear thinking and balanced judgement. This card speaks of truth, fairness and accountability. When Justice appears, the consequences of past actions are coming into view, and decisions should be made with honesty and care. It may point to legal matters, contracts or any situation where a fair outcome is needed. Justice asks you to see things as they are, without bias, and to take responsibility for your part. What is sown will be reaped, and integrity is its own protection. In its shadow the card can show unfairness, dishonesty or avoiding the truth. Justice reminds you that clarity is a kindness, and that a decision made in good conscience will stand the test of time.

12.short: Surrender, pause and a new perspective. The Hanged Man finds wisdom by letting go.
12.long: The Hanged Man hangs upside down by choice, calm and at peace, seeing the world from an unusual angle. This card speaks of surrender, waiting and a shift in perspective. When it appears, forcing an outcome will not work. Progress comes from letting go, pausing and looking at the situation in a completely new way. What looks like a delay may be a necessary stillness before understanding arrives. The card can also ask for a sacrifice: releasing an old belief, habit or expectation to make room for something truer. In its shadow it can point to stalling, indecision, or martyrdom with no purpose. The Hanged Man teaches that sometimes the most powerful thing you can do is nothing at all, and that wisdom often arrives upside down.

13.short: An ending that makes room for renewal. Death is transformation, the close of one chapter and the start of the next.
13.long: Death is one of the most misunderstood cards in the tarot. It rarely speaks of a physical death. Instead it marks transformation: the end of a chapter, a relationship, a way of life or a version of yourself. When Death appears, something has run its course, and holding on will only cause pain. Letting it go clears the ground for new growth. Endings can bring grief, and the card honours that, but it also carries the promise of renewal that follows every true release. This is a card of honesty about what is finished. In its shadow it can point to resistance to change, or to clinging to what is already gone. Death reminds you that transformation is the most natural thing in the world, and that every ending is also a door.

14.short: Balance, patience and the middle way. Temperance blends opposites into harmony.
14.long: Temperance pours water between two cups, mixing opposites into something new and balanced. This card speaks of moderation, patience and healing. When Temperance appears, you are asked to find the middle way: to avoid extremes, to combine different parts of your life with care and to give things the time they need. It is a card of calm progress rather than sudden leaps, and of recovery after difficulty. Relationships, health and plans all benefit from its steady, gentle touch. Temperance may also point to finding your purpose by bringing together your skills and values. In its shadow it can show excess, impatience or a life out of balance. Its lesson is that harmony is something you make, one careful measure at a time.

15.short: Attachment, temptation and the chains we choose. The Devil shows what holds you, and that you can leave.
15.long: The Devil is a card of attachment, desire and the things that bind us. It can point to unhealthy habits, materialism, or relationships and patterns that keep you from being free. Yet the chains in this card are often loose: what holds you may be held in place by fear or habit more than by force. When The Devil appears, look honestly at what controls you, and at the beliefs that keep you there. Naming a pattern is the first step to breaking it. The card can also speak of passion and the pull of pleasure, which are not wrong in themselves until they rule you. In its reversed or shadow sense it often marks release: the moment you realise you are free to walk away. The Devil asks you to reclaim your power.

16.short: Sudden change and revelation. The Tower brings down what was built on false ground, so the truth can stand.
16.long: The Tower is struck by lightning and its crown falls, a dramatic image of sudden upheaval. This card speaks of unexpected change, revelation and the collapse of structures that were never as solid as they seemed. When The Tower appears, something may break open quickly: a belief, a situation or an illusion you have been living with. It can feel shocking, but what falls was built on unstable ground. The lightning is also illumination, a flash of truth that shows things as they really are. After The Tower comes clear space to build again, on firmer foundations. In its shadow it can point to fear of change, or to avoiding a collapse that is already under way. The Tower teaches that sometimes destruction is the beginning of freedom.

17.short: Hope, healing and renewed faith. The Star shines after the storm and guides you gently forward.
17.long: The Star follows The Tower in the tarot, a quiet light after the storm. It is the card of hope, healing and renewed faith in the future. When The Star appears, the worst has passed and a period of calm and restoration is beginning. You are invited to rest, to recover and to trust that you are being guided. This is a card of inspiration and of reconnecting with your deepest wishes. It also speaks of openness and vulnerability, showing yourself as you truly are. The Star reminds you that you are part of something larger, and that your light matters. In its shadow it can point to discouragement, or to losing faith when the road is long. Its lesson is simple: keep hope alive, and let it lead you home.

18.short: Dreams, illusion and the unknown. The Moon lights a path through uncertainty, where intuition must guide you.
18.long: The Moon casts a pale, shifting light over a winding path, where nothing looks quite as it does by day. This card speaks of dreams, intuition, illusion and the hidden currents of the mind. When The Moon appears, things may be unclear, and fears or uncertainties may be stronger than usual. Not everything is as it seems, so move carefully, and trust your intuition over appearances. This is a card of the subconscious, where old memories, dreams and feelings rise to the surface to be understood. It can be a rich time for creativity and inner work. In its shadow it may point to confusion, deception or anxiety that clouds judgement. The Moon reminds you that the dark is not empty, and that the way through it is found by feeling, not by sight.

19.short: Joy, clarity and success. The Sun is warmth and vitality, a time to shine and be seen.
19.long: The Sun is one of the brightest cards in the tarot, radiating warmth, joy and confidence. It speaks of success, vitality and a clear understanding of yourself and your path. When The Sun appears, things are going well, or are about to, and you are encouraged to enjoy it fully. This is a time to be seen, to share your gifts and to celebrate what you have achieved. Relationships feel warm, plans move forward and energy is high. The card also carries a childlike sense of wonder, the simple happiness of being alive. In its shadow it can point to joy that has been dimmed, or to overconfidence that forgets others. The Sun reminds you that you deserve happiness, and that your light helps everyone around you to grow.

20.short: Awakening, reckoning and a calling answered. Judgement asks you to rise and become who you are meant to be.
20.long: Judgement is the card of awakening, when a call sounds and something long sleeping rises to answer it. It speaks of reflection, reckoning and renewal. When Judgement appears, you are being asked to look honestly at your life so far, to forgive what needs forgiving and to accept the lessons of the past. From that clarity comes a new beginning, often a sense of purpose or a calling you can no longer ignore. Decisions made now carry weight, and they should come from your truest self. The card may also mark a moment of being recognised for who you have become. In its shadow it can point to self judgement that is too harsh, or to ignoring a call out of fear. Judgement asks you to rise, and to step fully into your next chapter.

21.short: Completion, wholeness and arrival. The World closes the journey and opens the next.
21.long: The World is the final card of the Major Arcana, the moment the journey that began with The Fool comes full circle. It speaks of completion, achievement and wholeness. When The World appears, a cycle in your life is coming to a successful close, and you can feel the satisfaction of having arrived. Everything you have learned along the way is now part of you. This is a card of celebration, integration and harmony with the world around you. It may also point to travel, wider horizons or a sense of belonging. In its shadow it can show a goal almost reached, or a reluctance to let a chapter end. The World reminds you that every completion is also a beginning, and that the dance continues as a new journey begins.
